evidence: Across extraction_database.csv, 23 quasi-experimental rows (23 distinct study_design strings) match `grepl('experiment', ...)` and get misclassified into `experimental_only`, while the `observational+quasi-experimental` subset promised in L106 is never computed at all.
fix: Use `!grepl('quasi', study_design, ignore.case=TRUE) & grepl('experiment|randomi|\brct\b|trial', study_design, ignore.case=TRUE)` for `experimental_only`, and add explicit `obs_plus_quasi` subset.

issue: `rma(yi = effect_estimate, sei = standard_error)` pools raw `effect_estimate` across incompatible scales (OR, RR, IRR, probit, linear beta, percentage points) without scale check or back-transformation
evidence: In effect_sizes.csv (52 rows), `effect_measure` mixes OR, RR, HR, IRR, marginal probabilities, percentage points, and standardized betas; `01_meta_analysis.R` has no guard verifying homogeneous `effect_measure` within a family before calling `rma()`.
fix: Add an explicit assertion `length(unique(fam_data$effect_measure_scale)) == 1` before `rma()`, and log-transform ratio measures (`log(OR)` with delta-method SE) in a dedicated column.
